newsitem.title: USA: TWA pilots union files lawsuit vs airline.
newsitem.headline: TWA pilots union files lawsuit vs airline.

text.p: The union representating the pilots of Trans World Airlines Inc filed a lawsuit against the airline, contesting the calculation of certain pay and work rules.

The lawsuit, filed on behalf of the TWA pilots, resulted from TWA management's "recent notification that it intends to unilaterally impose new pay and work rules, which were not bargained with ALPA or even addressed by the recent arbitration rule," the union said in a prepared statement.

"Rather than comply with the arbitrator's decision to properly calculate monthly hours for the pilot group, TWA plans to unilaterally impose changes in the status quo, in violation of the Railway Labor Act," the union said in a statement.
The pilot's union, the Air Line Pilots Association, said it has offered TWA, the nation's seventh largest airline, several options that would satisfy the arbitrator's ruling.
TWA said it will abide by the arbitrator's ruling and is confident the arbitration ruling will be upheld.

"This is the result of the pilots taking a grievance to arbitration about how to calculate flying hours. The arbitrator made a decision .... It was a decision in favor of the pilot's position. And the pilots are deciding that they don't like it," said Mark Abels, a TWA spokesman said.
Separately, TWA and its pilots union began contract negotiations this week. The pilots' contract, which began September 1, 1994, becomes amendable on August 30.
